system.name: ZooRoute
system.one_liner: a cloud network reliability system that provisions candidate paths and proactively reroutes via an overlay when failures occur

components.name: CPU
components.role: issues path-table updates to the programmable ASIC

components.name: Hash Table
components.role: on-chip table storing {dstIP+index, srcPort} key-value pairs updated over PCIe

components.name: Programmable ASIC
components.role: hardware whose Hash Table is updated by the CPU over PCIe, limited by PCIe bandwidth

components.name: CPU
components.role: sends negotiation packets carrying PKT markers to update path state in-network

components.name: Hash Table
components.role: stores the relatively static mapping from destination IP to a register address

components.name: Register
components.role: stores frequently changing source-port status, read/written at line rate during packet processing

components.name: Programmable ASIC
components.role: Tofino ASIC that extracts header fields from update packets, rewrites the matching entry, and recirculates the packet for the next update

components.name: Endflag
components.role: marker on the last update packet in a batch that stops the recirculation loop

content.key_idea: ZooRoute replaces PCIe-pushed path-table updates, which are bandwidth-limited, with an in-network mechanism where negotiation packets update a hash table and per-port registers directly on the Tofino ASIC, batching updates per packet via recirculation.
content.reading_order: Top panel (a) shows the naive CPU-over-PCIe update; bottom panel (b) shows ZooRoute's packet-driven update, read left to right following circled steps 1-3.

summary: This figure compares two ways ZooRoute's programmable ASIC receives path-table updates. In (a), a naive baseline, the CPU pushes {dstIP+index, srcPort} key-value updates into an on-chip Hash Table over PCIe, whose bandwidth limits update concurrency. In (b), ZooRoute's design, the CPU instead sends negotiation packets carrying PKT markers into the Programmable ASIC/Tofino (step 1); the ASIC looks up the destination IP in a Hash Table to get a register address and updates the corresponding source-port entry in a Register array (step 2); it then invalidates the processed header and recirculates the packet to handle the next batched update, repeating until an Endflag is reached (step 3). A small legend marks the packet-delivered-update line style and the Endflag marker.
summary_zh: 对比两种更新ZooRoute路径表的方式：(a) CPU经PCIe直接写哈希表，带宽受限；(b) 改用协商数据包，按①②③查表更新寄存器源端口，循环注入报文处理下一条更新，直到Endflag。
notes: The extracted crop for this figure also contains a 'log2(Np) bit' register-encoding table on the far left (Null/00010/00001 rows) that is not mentioned in the Fig. 13 text and whose position suggests it actually belongs to the adjacent Figure 12 (its bbox spans the same page row); it is excluded from components/flows above.
